name: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd
about: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd is engaged in the business of manufacturing, developing and marketing a wide range of branded and generic formulations and Active Pharma Ingredients (APIs). The company and its subsidiaries has various manufacturing facilities spread across the world with trading and other incidental and related activities extending to global market. [1] It is the largest pharmaceutical company in India. [2]

sections.one_liner: India's largest pharma, shifting to innovative medicines; the debt-funded Organon deal, which doubles revenue, now drives the equity story.
business: Makes branded generics, generics, APIs and innovative medicines across 100+ countries and 40 manufacturing facilities; #1 in India, 13th in US generics. [AR FY26]
Innovative Medicines are 22% of sales, focused on dermatology, ophthalmology and onco-derm; FY26 US$1,420m, up 16.8%. [AR FY26] [Q4FY26 call]
Geographic mix: India 32.3%, US 27.5%, Emerging Markets 19.4%; US innovative medicines now exceed US generics revenue. [Q3FY26 call] [AR FY26]
Organon deal: pro forma revenue $12.4bn vs Sun's $6.2bn, adding women's health and biosimilars across 150+ markets. [M&A call Apr26]
financial_snapshot: Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026): revenue Rs15,300cr, +10.5% YoY; PAT Rs2,901cr, +26.5% YoY, flattered by weak base of Rs2,293cr. [Numbers]
Q1 OPM 29% vs 31% a year ago, despite gross margin of 80.5%; opex is absorbing the mix gain. [Numbers] [Q1FY27 call]
TTM: revenue Rs59,911cr, EBITDA Rs17,847cr (29.8% margin), PAT Rs12,117cr. [Numbers]
Valuation: P/E 34.4x, P/B 5.2x (Rs1,814 vs book Rs348), ROCE 20.5%, ROE 16.0%, dividend yield 0.9%. [Numbers]
trajectory: Revenue CAGR is 11.8% over 5 years and 10.0% over 3 years; FY26 growth of 11.2% reaccelerated from FY25's 8.4%. [Numbers]
PAT 5-year CAGR of 38.3% reflects a low FY21 base of Rs2,272cr; the 3-year CAGR of 10.6% just tracks revenue. [Numbers]
OPM rose from 25% (FY21) to 29% (FY25), then slipped to 28% in FY26; Q4 FY26 hit 27%. [Numbers]
ROCE rose from 13% to 21% over 5 years; net worth climbed from Rs55,995cr to Rs83,570cr, while cash dilutes ROE to 16%. [Numbers]
balance_sheet: Borrowings nearly doubled to Rs4,627cr in FY26 from Rs2,362cr; D/E is 0.06, against net cash of $3.4bn. [Numbers] [Q1FY27 call]
After Organon, net debt/EBITDA is guided at 2.3x, a swing from net cash to the first material leverage. [M&A call Apr26]
Cash conversion cycle fell from 310 to 228 days since FY21; inventory days remain 363 and debtor days rose from 85 to 97. [Numbers]
cash_quality: CFO/PAT averaged 1.2x over 3 years, but slipped to 1.08x in FY26 from 1.28x in FY25. [Numbers]
FCF fell 26% to Rs8,906cr in FY26 as implied capex rose to Rs3,513cr from Rs2,067cr. [Numbers]
FY26 FCF is 0.77x PAT; profits convert to cash, but the conversion is weakening ahead of Organon funding needs. [Numbers]
narrative_vs_numbers: Agree on India: sales up 16% on 5.4% volume growth (IPM 2%), so roughly 10pp comes from price, mix and launches. [Q1FY27 call]
Diverge on margin: gross margin rose to 80.5%, yet OPM fell 2pp YoY to 29%; the mix story is not reaching EBITDA. [Q1FY27 call] [Numbers]
FY26 EBITDA is Rs17,731cr (30.3%) per the call vs Rs16,501cr (28%) in Numbers; adjusted PAT Rs12,402cr vs reported Rs11,509cr. [Q4FY26 call] [Numbers]
Innovative growth is slowing: 16.8% in FY26, 14.3% in Q3, 12.8% in Q1 FY27; US sales fell 9.7% to $427m. [Q4FY26 call] [Q1FY27 call]
guidance: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at high single digit, below FY26's 11.9%; reiterated in the Q1 call. [Q4FY26 call] [Q1FY27 call]
FY27 R&D guided at 6-7% of sales, up from 6.1% in FY26, with a rising innovative share. [Q4FY26 call] [AR FY26]
Tax rate guided at 25% in May, then reset to the Q1 level of 27.8% until Organon closes. [Q4FY26 call] [Q1FY27 call]
Organon close targeted for Q4 FY27; deal-related charges are back-ended and mostly accrued at closing. [Q1FY27 call]
Organon deal: $350m cost synergies over 2-4 years, EPS accretive in year one, combined FCF of $2.0-2.5bn. [M&A call Apr26]

ledger.delivered: Q1 tax rate 27.8%; guidance reset upward until Organon closes

ledger.delivered: OPM recovered from 27% to 29%, still below 31-32% in Q2-Q3 FY26

ledger.promised: Three new US generic launches next quarter [Q3FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Two US generics plus UNLOXCYT launched in Q4 (call disclosure; not in Numbers)

ledger.promised: Day-one semaglutide launch in India [Q3FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: Launched in Q4; #2 generic player by Q1 FY27; day-one timing not disclosed

ledger.promised: Organon acquisition closes in Q4 FY27 [M&A call Apr26] [Q1FY27 call]
ledger.delivered: Not yet due; reiterated in Q1 FY27 call

bull: India is compounding: 16% growth, share up to 8.5%, volume 5.4% vs IPM 2%, #1 in 12 therapy areas. [Q1FY27 call]
Organon lifts innovative mix from 20% to 27%, with $350m synergies and EPS accretion from year one. [M&A call Apr26]
ROCE has expanded to 21% with 3-year CFO/PAT of 1.2x and net cash of $3.4bn before the deal. [Numbers] [Q1FY27 call]
bear: 34.4x P/E for a high single-digit growth guide, while the tax rate rises 2.8pp above earlier guidance. [Numbers] [Q1FY27 call]
Organon grows only 1-2% organically and adds 2.3x leverage; synergies are about 5.6% of its ~$6.2bn revenue. [M&A call Apr26]
US generics are shrinking: US sales down 9.7%, approvals stalled by compliance, and FY26 FCF down 26%. [Q1FY27 call] [Numbers]
questions: Gross margin is 80.5%, yet OPM is down 2pp YoY; what is the opex trajectory?
Why did the tax rate move to 27.8% from the 25% guided just ten weeks earlier?
What is the total Organon transaction charge, and how much falls in FY27?
Which sites must clear compliance before US generic approvals resume, and when?

annual_report.business: Global pharmaceutical company serving 100+ countries. Develops, manufactures and distributes innovative medicines, branded generics, generics, APIs and consumer healthcare products. Largest pharma in India; 13th largest US generics company.

segments.comment: Specialty focus: dermatology, ophthalmology, onco-dermatology. Strategic priority

segments.name: US Business
segments.comment: Growing Innovative Medicines now exceed generics share of US revenue

segments.name: India
segments.comment: Market leader with 8.4% share. Volume-led growth driver

segments.name: Emerging Markets

annual_report.revenue_mix: 67% international from established operations. Innovative Medicines 22% of total. Volume-led India growth. Specialty medicines increasingly valuable globally.
strategy: Advance Innovative Medicines in dermatology, ophthalmology, onco-dermatology via R&D and acquisitions
Expand global reach via Organon acquisition adding Women's Health therapeutic pillar
Maintain cost leadership while investing 6.1% of sales in R&D for innovation
Build manufacturing resilience across 40 facilities with quality focus
Balance long-term innovation with near-term profitability across geographies
annual_report.outlook: Global pharma market reaching US$2.4T by 2029 (CAGR 5-8%). India market growth 6.5-9.5% CAGR. Organon acquisition enhancing global scale and Women's Health portfolio. Specialty medicines driving value. Focus on clinical differentiation addressing unmet needs.
annual_report.capex_plans: Ongoing investment in 40 global manufacturing facilities, 6 R&D centers and digital capabilities. Organon acquisition expanding manufacturing footprint and regional presence.
risks: MFN pricing from 2026 creating downward price pressure and near-term market uncertainty
Loss of Exclusivity intensifying: US$179B projected erosion over 5 years vs US$49B prior
Section 232 tariff investigations on pharma products, APIs, critical inputs pending outcomes
Regulatory complexity, geopolitical uncertainty and supply chain unpredictability
annual_report.flags: Leadership transition: Kirti Ganorkar appointed Managing Director; Dilip Shanghvi continues as Executive Chairman. Organon acquisition announced post-FY26, subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals.
